posts.author: Kabir_B
posts.text: Which five numbers should you review regularly to understand your financial health, and how often should you check them? — I think one number people probably underestimate is their monthly burn rate. Knowing your net worth is great, but knowing exactly how much it costs to maintain your current lifestyle tells you a lot more about how financially comfortable you actually are. For me, I would track : Monthly expenses/burn rate. Liquid cash available. Total debt + EMI burden. Invested assets. Net worth. And I wouldn’t check everything every week. Expenses and liquid cash can be monitored monthly…

posts.author: RajendraPatil
posts.text: Which is a better option for investing in gold: Gold ETF, Gold ETF FoF, or Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs)? — correct ! one can look at it from different perspective. SGBs cant be re-invested once matured. it means for long term SGB will not exist. Gold ETF : in long term you may have large sums, and while offloading you may have to face impact cost. Gold FoF: Additional layer of costs can pinch in long run So only option 2 and 3 are available for long term investors Personally today, I prefer to pay additional fees to mutual fund and invest in FoFs, its personal choice.

posts.author: pothi
posts.text: Which is a better option for investing in gold: Gold ETF, Gold ETF FoF, or Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs)? — An AI could have given better answer, but IMO, between Gold ETFs and Gold ETF FoFs, it depends on your time and style of investing. When I used to have a lot of time, I used to order/buy ETFs in smaller quantities at a rate less than iNAV by checking iNAV regularly. Nowadays, I order through FoF, even it means an increased / double expense ratio. I can still place AMO through ETF. I might be buying at a higher rate at times.
